claims.evidence: MedlinePlus summary: a normal oxygen saturation level ranges between 95% and 100%; lower may be acceptable with lung disease such as COPD. NHS England diary: 'An ideal blood oxygen level is between 95% and 100%'.

BTS: for COPD or other risk factors for hypercapnic respiratory failure aim at 88-92% pending blood gas results (adjust to 94-98% if PCO2 satisfactory); the BTS COPD admission bundle repeats 94-98% vs 88-92% 'at risk of CO2 retention'.

Medical Gases Learning Package (UHD, April 2020): type 1 respiratory failure = hypoxic failure without hypercapnia, PaO2 below 8 kPa; type 2 = with hypercapnia. 'On air/room air' wording came from other retrieved sources (PaO2 <60 mmHg (8 kPa) on room air, normal or low PaCO2), not verifiably from the UHD excerpt. Old text 'below 8 kPa defines respiratory failure' (type-less) was imprecise; the edit is correct.

Interpretation 'Low SpO2 on air' row: BTS 94-98% default / 88-92% if at risk of retention. NHS England documents: recheck, and if still 92% or below go to A&E or call 999; 93-94% prompts contacting a clinician. 'NHS 111 or the GP the same day' for the non-emergency route is consistent. Number removed from finding label, which is acceptable.

Record 1 (95 to 100 %, UK, NHS England diary): diary excerpt says ideal blood oxygen is 95-100%. Context clause 'people with long-term lung disease may run lower even when well': carried by MedlinePlus (lower levels may be acceptable in COPD/pneumonia) and one NHS document (usual level below 95% -> drop from own baseline); the diary page itself was not shown to say it. Section label 'Pulse oximeter readings' could not be verified as the diary's heading.
Record 2 (95 to 100 %, US, MedlinePlus): normal 95-100%; 'results may be 2% to 4% higher or lower than your actual blood oxygen level'. US jurisdiction appropriate. Section 'Results' reasonable.

Record 3 (88 to 92 %, UK, BTS): 88-92% pending blood gases in COPD/other hypercapnic-risk patients; 94-98% initial target for most acutely ill adults. URL is the guideline page; section 'Target saturation' reasonable.

Record 4 (below 8 kPa, UK, UHD): package defines type 1 failure as PaO2 below 8 kPa without hypercapnia; type 2 by hypercapnia. The unit text 'PaO2 on air' and context 'on room air' match definitions in other retrieved sources but the UHD excerpt itself was garbled; section label 'Respiratory failure' unverified but reasonable. Note the package is a 2020 hospital training document, not a national guideline; BTS (c07 URL) is the stronger citation for oxygen targets, and Thorax/BTS text also uses 8 kPa.

notes: 17 searches shared across the three ids (about 6 for this id). All changed text supported. Record 4's UHD page is a 2020 hospital learning package; search excerpt was jumbled, so wording 'on air' rests on corroborating sources. NHS England diary section label not verified. BTS notes a possible update under consideration; check current version.
